text:
laura_sales: FYI demo with Tim (prospect) just hit a streaming hiccup. SSE feed cut out about 30–45s in, client threw a parsing error and stopped rendering. can we swarm?
evan_eng: on it. any logs from the client or our side?
tim_prospect: from my side the app shows "Unexpected end of input while parsing event". happens a couple times, sometimes recovers on reconnect. saw a 502 from the load balancer once.
laura_sales: logged it with the prospect — they said it was intermittent, worse on longer responses. they were trying the summarization flow with ~1200 token outputs.
maria_sre: pinging infra. can you paste the raw SSE fragment the client received? even a partial dump helps.
tim_prospect: here's what I copied from the browser console network tab (truncated):
```
data: {"chunk": "\"Hello, I'm a long response that ...\""}\n\

data: {"chunk": "\"continued text...\""}\n\

data: {
```
then it stops — last chunk incomplete.
evan_eng: that looks like the server closed mid-event. two possibilities: proxy buffering or server-side flush not happening, or we're hitting a connection reset (rate limit / upstream).
evan_eng: @maria_sre can you check the gateway/NLB logs around 1802509876-1802509950 for any connection resets or backend 5xx spikes?
maria_sre: checking now. I see a few `502` and `504` entries correlated with that timeframe from the edge, plus a TCP FIN shortly after some client streams. forwarding trace ids.
maria_sre: edge notes: `proxy_buffering on` missing flush hints; nginx is allowed to buffer ~8k chunks. if the runtime isn't flushing small events, proxy may coalesce and then truncate on connection churn.
evan_eng: useful. two engineering actions: 1) add explicit SSE framing flush (ensure each `data:` event ends with `\n\n` and call flush) and 2) set `Cache-Control: no-transform` and `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` with small chunk writes. also set `X-Accel-Buffering: no` if going through nginx.
laura_sales: can you roll a quick patch we can push to the POC endpoint? Prospect wants a patch quickly, even if it's a temporary mitigation.
evan_eng: I can patch the POC service to flush after each chunk. sample Node change:
```
// before
res.write(`data: ${json}\n\n`);
// after - force immediate flush
res.write(`data: ${json}\n\n`);
res.flushHeaders();
if (res.flush) res.flush();
```
Should also ensure gzip is disabled for streaming endpoints.
tim_prospect: any client-side workarounds while you patch? we can't change prod user app quickly.
evan_eng: on the client, make the SSE parser tolerant: buffer partial `data:` lines until you see the terminating `\n\n`. also retry on parse errors and handle `last-event-id`. quick patch in the browser:
```
// naive reassembly example
let buffer = '';
source.onmessage = (e) => { /* existing */ };
source.addEventListener('message', (e) => { /* normally fine */ });
source.onmessageerror = (err) => {
  // try to reconnect with last-event-id
  source.close();
  setTimeout(() => startSSE(lastEventId), 300);
};
```
maria_sre: infra temporary tweak: set `proxy_buffering off; proxy_read_timeout 90s;` on the path for the POC host, and disable gzip for that vhost. I can apply a canary change.
damian_sales: I told the prospect we'd have an engineer on the call in 30m and we could push a mitigation. timeline ok?
evan_eng: yes can push small flush change in 10–15m, roll to the POC slot. I'll also add header toggles so we can revert.
laura_sales: perfect — also FYI prospect asked about Dedicated capacity for stability and higher QPS. they want ballpark pricing now.
evan_eng: for long-running streaming workloads we recommend Dedicated GPU pool; rough numbers: starting commit $12k/mo for baseline, up to $40k+/mo for sustained large throughput. I'll let sales provide exact sizing after we see request rate.
laura_sales: @damian_sales can you follow up with pricing sheet after we confirm avg req/sec from the POC logs?
damian_sales: yep. I'll wait for maria to post the qps numbers.
maria_sre: qps for that 10m window was ~18 req/min to the streaming endpoint from that customer, but bursts up to 6 concurrent streams. token output per stream was high which increases bandwidth and chance of fragmentation.
evan_eng: another angle: enable server-side smaller chunk sizes (e.g., 256–512 bytes) so clients reassemble more predictably. also consider an option to emit sentinel `event: chunk-end` events so client knows the boundary even if a chunk is partial.
laura_sales: prospect also flagged security: they asked about SOC2 and SSO integration for Private deployments. can someone send the standard packet?
damian_sales: I'll attach the security one-pager and SOC2 attestation doc after this thread; getting SSO/SCIM details is part of the next call.
tim_prospect: thanks all. if you can push a patch and we retry the demo, we'll go from there.
evan_eng: patch deployed to POC host (canary) at 1802510010: added flush + `X-Accel-Buffering: no` and disabled gzip. can you retest?
tim_prospect: re-ran the flow — looks much better, no parse error after 3 runs. will stress for a bit and report back. :+1:
maria_sre: left the proxy change in canary for 15m, watching metrics. no 5xx or FINs seen in the next 5m sample.
laura_sales: huge — I'll update the prospect and capture any remaining asks. follow-ups: pricing doc, SOC2 packet, and the option to discuss Dedicated sizing. thanks team! :rocket:
